prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
This document sets out recent outcomes and plans for 2005–2010 across the economy, public services, security, families, the environment, international policy and democratic reform.

Economy and jobs
- Keep the 2% inflation target and fiscal rules; pursue efficiency savings to invest in frontline services; no rises in basic or top income tax rates and no VAT on essentials.
- Target high employment (aiming for an 80% rate) via welfare-to-work, reform of Incapacity Benefit (Pathways to Work), higher minimum wage, and use of independent/voluntary partners.
- Support enterprise and manufacturing (including through public procurement), expand apprenticeships, and implement a 10‑year science and innovation strategy to raise total R&D to 2.5% of GDP by 2014.
- Energy policy to combine renewables, nuclear, clean coal and microgeneration; streamline planning; improve consumer protections (payments, dormant accounts).

Transport and regions
- Invest over £180bn in transport to 2015; improve rail reliability, consider high‑speed rail (including North–South link) and Crossrail; targeted motorway capacity; explore national road pricing; free off‑peak local bus travel for over‑60s and disabled people.
- Regional development, local enterprise growth incentives, and neighbourhood renewal in deprived areas.

Education and skills
- More personalised learning; guaranteed per‑pupil funding increases via a national schools budget; stronger parental engagement and Ofsted response.
- Primary literacy/numeracy targets; nationwide renewal of school buildings; all secondary schools to be specialist, with at least 200 Academies by 2010; tougher discipline and fair admissions.
- 14–19 reform with vocational diplomas, more apprenticeships and EMAs; FE modernisation and skills academies.
- Higher education: increased funding with variable fees capped at £3,000 (plus grants and bursaries), aim for 50% participation, more PhD support.

Health and social care
- Higher NHS investment, more staff, shorter waits; by 2008 a maximum 18 weeks from GP referral to treatment and free choice of hospital.
- Expand primary/community services and community hospitals; practice‑based commissioning; use independent/voluntary providers to add capacity.
- Reduce hospital infections; strengthen clinical governance; publish clinical trial results.
- Public health: improve school food standards, clearer food labelling, restrict marketing of high fat/salt/sugar products to children, extend smoke‑free workplaces with defined exceptions; expand cessation services and health trainers.
- Integrate health and social care; expand dentistry and review provision.

Crime, borders and security
- Neighbourhood policing teams nationwide; more Community Support Officers; single non‑emergency number.
- Wider powers against antisocial behaviour; alcohol disorder zones; youth justice improvements.
- Expand drug testing/treatment linked to offending; establish the Serious Organised Crime Agency; restructure police capabilities.
- Tighter controls on knives and replica guns; sentencing and reoffending reforms; asset recovery expanded; corporate manslaughter offence.
- Points‑based immigration system prioritising skills; English for settlement; penalties for illegal employment; streamlined appeals; biometric visas/ID cards linked to passports; e‑borders.
- New powers to disrupt terrorism; strengthened international cooperation.

Families, housing and older people
- Halve child poverty by 2010–11 through work, tax credits and the Child Trust Fund.
- Universal childcare expansion: 3,500 Sure Start Children’s Centres; 15 hours/week free nursery for 3–4‑year‑olds (towards 20); extended schools 8am–6pm; more childcare support.
- Maternity leave to nine months (aim for 12); extend flexible working rights (including for carers).
- Increase home ownership (including shared ownership); raise stamp duty threshold; more and better social housing, choice‑based lettings, bring empty homes into use.
- Pension Credit, fuel support and free off‑peak bus travel; plan long‑term pensions reform; flexible retirement rights; pilot individual care budgets.

Environment, culture and digital
- Lead on climate change (CO2 reduction targets; renewables; emissions trading).
- Cleaner neighbourhoods; universal kerbside recycling for two materials by 2010; brownfield‑first development; sustainable building code; Marine Act.
- Free entry to national museums; expand arts/sport participation; support the 2012 Olympics legacy; modernise libraries.
- Digital switchover 2008–2012 with support for vulnerable users; BBC governance reform; modernise IP and film tax relief.

International and democracy
- Active role in EU reform (referendum on Constitutional Treaty), cautious euro policy; non‑proliferation; support for Iraq transition and Middle East peace; modernise armed forces and retain nuclear deterrent; UN, World Bank and IMF reforms.
- Increase aid to 0.7% of national income by 2013; debt relief; governance and anti‑corruption; universal access to AIDS treatment by 2010; fairer trade and CAP reform.
- Complete House of Lords reform; strengthen equality and human rights framework; further devolution (Wales, London, regions); restore Northern Ireland institutions; greater local powers, council freedoms, and council tax restraint.
